statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail risk is low with cash equities and index futures closed for the weekend.
recommendation: Tail remains well below the block threshold throughout the weekend halt. The elevated Stress reading describes a persistent energy and long-end yield backdrop rather than an observed one-way Nasdaq-100 path, and the first opportunity for new price-path evidence is the Sunday futures reopen at 22:00Z, which falls outside this forecast window.
headline: Nasdaq-100 in weekend halt: Tail low after Friday's record probe faded, energy and long-end stress persist
body: Friday's session closed the Nasdaq-100 at 30,807.93, up 1.00%, after probing an intraday record near 31,017.53 and then retracing roughly 0.7% into the close. September payrolls of 29,000 against expectations near 85,000, with unemployment at 4.2% and average hourly earnings up 0.1% on the month, cut priced odds of an October rate hike to roughly 16% from about 64% a week earlier and drove a tech-led advance. VIX fell about 6.6% to 15.31. The macro backdrop nevertheless remains difficult: the 10-year yield rose to 5.28% and the 30-year sat near 5.63%, Brent held near $102.25 and WTI near $91.11, and a diesel squeeze that lifted U.S. diesel prices about 70% since late February to around $6.37 a gallon prompted a G7 agreement to release up to 100 million barrels over four months. The Iran conflict and Strait of Hormuz shipping risk remain unresolved, with a tanker struck on Friday. Because index futures have been shut since Friday 21:00Z and do not restart until 22:00Z on Sunday, no live price path can develop anywhere inside this 24-hour forecast. Friday's completed retracement from the session high, a low VIX and the absence of an active tape keep Tail in the low band, while persistent energy and long-end pressure hold Stress in the elevated band. The shared Finviz context was stale at run time and was not used as current evidence.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours span Friday's payroll session and the start of the weekend halt. Tail sat in the watch band through the European morning, rose to 25 and then 27 around the 12:30Z payroll release and the 13:30Z cash open as the index gapped up and extended, and fell back into the watch band once the advance faded from its intraday high. From 21:00Z, with futures closed, Tail declined steadily from 14 to 8 while Stress eased from the high band to 65 and the dominant mode settled to normal.
outlookSummary: All 24 forecast hours fall inside the CME weekend halt, since index futures closed on Friday at 21:00Z and do not restart until 22:00Z on Sunday, beyond this horizon. With no mechanism for mean-reversion failure on a closed tape, Tail is projected to hold between 6 and 8 and the mapped state stays EA_ON throughout. Stress eases from 62 toward 58 as realised volatility goes to zero, then edges back toward 60 as the new week approaches with Brent above $100 and the 30-year near 5.63%. Confidence decays from 85 to 78 as Friday's settled dataset ages without any possible refresh. The first genuine checkpoints are the Sunday reopen gap and Monday's services data.

forecast.analysis: Observed: CME equity-index futures have been shut since Friday 21:00Z, and Friday's cash session probed an intraday record near 31,017.53 before closing back at 30,807.93. That completed retracement, alongside VIX at 15.31, keeps Tail low. Stress at 62 carries Brent near $102 and a 5.28% 10-year yield.
